root_cause.text: The hugetlb memory-failure path held hugetlb_lock across __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison()’s error cleanup, where folio_put() could drop the last reference on a hugetlb folio and invoke free_huge_folio(), recursively re-acquiring the same non-recursive hugetlb_lock and deadlocking.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “the out: path in __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() calls folio_put() ... while the hugetlb_lock is still held,” and the patch fixes it by removing the hugetlb.c wrapper that locked around the call and instead adding spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock) before the folio_put() in mm/memory-failure.c.

intent_record.how: At runtime this removes the fallback no-op definition from this compilation path, so callers can no longer resolve to an always-success stub here and must instead use another available definition or fail to compile if none exists; this prevents this code path from silently claiming success without doing any work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the exported declaration of `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison` to reduce the exposed interface and keep the header consistent with intended symbol visibility.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the extern declaration of the function `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(unsigned long pfn, int flags, bool *migratable_cleared);` from the header/interface section, while leaving the surrounding memory failure and poisoned page declarations unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not directly change execution behavior; functionally it narrows the visible API by no longer exposing that symbol through this declaration, which helps prevent or reflect the elimination of external use of the function and aligns the interface with its actual intended scope.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the no-op __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison fallback stub to avoid masking missing huge-page hwpoison handling with an unconditional success return.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the static inline stub definition of __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(unsigned long pfn, int flags, bool *migratable_cleared) that previously returned 0 in this conditional compilation fallback section.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the local no-op fallback implementation so this configuration no longer provides that stub from this header section, preventing callers from silently receiving a success-like return value from an empty implementation and forcing use of another definition or surfacing missing support at build time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() wrapper that only locked hugetlb_lock and forwarded to __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison().
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() function definition, including its local variable, the spin_lock_irq()/spin_unlock_irq() calls around hugetlb_lock, the call to __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(), and the return of its result.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a wrapper entry point that acquired hugetlb_lock and delegated to __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(). Callers can no longer use this exported path, implying the locking-wrapped helper is being removed in favor of other code paths or direct handling elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make hugetlb hwpoison page lookup self-locking so folio inspection happens under `hugetlb_lock` and early exits unlock correctly.
intent_record.what: The function `__get_huge_page_for_hwpoison` was renamed to `get_huge_page_for_hwpoison`, changed from non-static to `static`, its preceding comment stating it is called with `hugetlb_lock` held was removed, a delayed declaration `struct folio *folio;` replaced the immediate initialization `struct folio *folio = page_folio(page);`, and a new `spin_lock_irq(&hugetlb_lock);` was added before resolving the folio; the early non-hugetlb exit target was also changed from `out` to `out_unlock`.
intent_record.how: The function now acquires `hugetlb_lock` itself before inspecting the page's folio and ensures the early return path releases that lock, so callers no longer need to hold the lock externally and the hugetlb page check executes under proper synchronization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix early-exit paths in __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() to unlock properly before returning.
intent_record.what: In __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(), two goto targets were changed: the branch taken when MF_NO_RETRY is not set now jumps from out to out_unlock, and the branch taken when hugetlb_update_hwpoison() returns rc >= MF_HUGETLB_FOLIO_PRE_POISONED also jumps from out to out_unlock instead of out.
intent_record.how: These early-exit paths now follow the cleanup path that performs unlocking before returning, preventing the function from leaving a lock held when retry or pre-poisoned conditions cause an early exit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release hugetlb_lock on all return paths in __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison to fix a missing unlock bug.
intent_record.what: A spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock) call was added immediately before the normal return path, the existing error label was renamed from out to out_unlock, and that label now also performs spin_unlock_irq(&hugetlb_lock) before the folio_put(folio) cleanup and return.
intent_record.how: This ensures hugetlb_lock is released on both the successful return path and the cleanup path, preventing the function from returning while still holding the spinlock with interrupts disabled, which could otherwise cause lockups or incorrect locking state.

consistency_review.core_intent: Internalize and simplify the hugetlb hwpoison page lookup API by removing the redundant public wrapper and cleaning up its related interface declarations.
Fix hugetlb hardware-poison page lookup/handling by removing misleading no-op fallback stubs and ensuring hugetlb_lock is correctly managed on all lookup paths.

relevance_review.reason: The removed wrapper is the code that took hugetlb_lock around __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(); that locking pattern is central to the deadlock root cause. Internalizing/removing this API directly touches the vulnerable path rather than being a purely cosmetic refactor.

The group directly changes __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() and hugetlb_lock handling in the hugetlb hwpoison path, including fixing lock management on return/error paths. Since the root cause is a deadlock caused by holding hugetlb_lock during hwpoison cleanup, these changes are directly tied to that vulnerable code path.

candidates.rationale: This call is made while hugetlb_lock is held by the wrapper, causing __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() error cleanup to execute under the lock; if folio_put() drops the last reference, free_huge_folio() recursively re-acquires hugetlb_lock and deadlocks.
The wrapper acquires hugetlb_lock before invoking __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(), which is the core locking mistake behind the deadlock during cleanup.

In the error path, folio_put() may drop the final reference and trigger free_huge_folio(); when reached while the caller still holds hugetlb_lock, this leads to recursive lock acquisition and deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires hugetlb_lock in the wrapper before calling into __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison(). That causes the callee's error cleanup to run while hugetlb_lock is still held, enabling recursive re-acquisition through folio_put() -> free_huge_folio() and thus the deadlock described in the root cause.

This call is made under the hugetlb_lock acquired by the wrapper. As a result, if __get_huge_page_for_hwpoison() hits its error path and executes folio_put(), the final put may invoke free_huge_folio(), which tries to take hugetlb_lock again and deadlocks.
